EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  NOVEMBER 26, 2018

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL called the meeting to order, the time being 7:02 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Judy Mitchell
Susan Brtis
Bill Kemp
Lou Persichina
Carrie Silvano
Vicki Shinn

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT
Patricia Harik
Carol Dean-Porter
Tim Zigrang

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 24, 2018
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE SEPTEMBER 24, 2018 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
Diane Rudolf submitted a proposed fencing diagram to the Equestrian Committee to make
equestrians safer at the intersections of Palos Verdes Drive North at Crenshaw and
Hawthorne Boulevards. CHAIRMAN MITCHELL asked the Community Services Director to
provide the diagram to the Assistant City Manager for the City’s Traffic Engineer and/or the
Traffic and Safety Committee’s consideration.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
NOVEMBER 26, 2018  1
 CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT MONTHLY
UPDATE
Korey Bradbury from California Water Service Company distributed project update fact sheets
and highlighted the progress made thus far. He indicated that most of the work was currently
taking place on the Palomino Ranchos Trail and that preparations were underway to start the

Botanical Gardens Trial and Lariat Lane sections of the new pipeline. Several audience
members provided positive comments about the project and in response to CHAIRMAN
MITCHELL’S inquiry, he indicated that most Boarders would likely be able to return to their
regular boarding facilities around the end of January.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL THANKED MR. BRADBURY AND
RECEIVED AND FILED THIS AGENDA ITEM.

HOWLETT PARK RIDING CLINIC CONFLICTS WITH ADJACENT ARENA USERS
Local boarder, Diane Rudolf, informed the Committee that she was asked not to turn out her
two horses on November 8, 2018 in the rectangular warm-up arena at Ernie Howlett Park.
The organizer of a Jumping Clinic in Arena #1 and Terry Griggs, who was taking a lesson in
the Dressage Arena both told her she could not turn out her horses until both were done using
the adjacent arenas to the warm-up arena. She used the park’s lower lunging arena instead.

Committee Members concurred that unless a Clinic organizer or licensed Horse Trainer
rented all the upper arenas at Ernie Howlett Park that it was inappropriate for the public to not
have access to these unused arenas. The Community Services Director suggested that a
Subcommittee be formed to develop rules for use of the Howlett Park horse arenas by Clinic
organizers and licensed Horse Trainers. He suggested that these arenas users, when asked,
be required to allow equestrians to turn out their horses for ten minutes. Diane Rudolf and
Members Brtis, Kemp, Silvano, and Shinn volunteered to be on the Subcommittee and meet
prior to the January 28, 2018 Equestrian Committee Meeting to develop recommendations.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

EQUINE MICROCHIP HOLIDAY EVENT
MEMBER SHINN reported that there will be a horse chipping clinic at Ernie Howlett Park on
Sunday, December 9, 2018 by the LA County Animal Care & Control Department. The
Community Services Director noted that this will be open to all LA County residents.
MEMBER SHINN noticed that the event flyer did not have the location or cost and asked the
Community Services Director to notify the Chipping Clinic organizer to revise this flyer.

MEMBER SHINN also asked the Community Services Director to set up an Equine
Emergency Preparedness Subcommittee meeting to discuss resident equine evacuation
plans.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
NOVEMBER 26, 2018  2
 THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
In response to CHAIRMAN MITCHELL’S inquiry, the Community Services Director state that
during the clearing of brush from the region of the Ferncreek Trail, that asphalt chips had
inadvertently been removed, but were recently replaced.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS

MEMBER SHINN reported that there was broken glass on the trail near Carol Dean-Porter’s
home.

MEMBER KEMP indicated that a thick layer of Pine needles on the trail near the General
Store was a fire safety concern. He also reported that he had completed ERT Level 1.

MEMBER BRTIS recommended that the City implement Red Flag Days to restrict all vehicles
from the City’s trails.

CHAIRMAN MITCHELL suggested that a procedure be developed for trail riders to report
areas of dead brush for removal by the City.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE – Monthly

B.  EQUINE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN UPDATE – Monthly

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 8:00 p.m.

NOVEMBER 26, 2018  3
 Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
